source.title: Detecting noisy labels using checkpoint ensembles

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and tables are garbled or flattened, but the relevant training result is stated in text.
record.tranche_reason: Reports whether training on noisy CIFAR-100 labels eventually memorizes the training set, bearing on the training-error claim, but does not report exact training-error values.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports many noisy-label detection and filtering metrics. Those do not measure the claim's training-error outcome and are not included as rows. Results cited from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: Section 6 reports the study's own SGD training trajectories and eventual training-set memorization for a convolutional network on corrupted-label CIFAR-100, directly bearing on V1 using the same training method and outcome as the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Carefully selected checkpoint ensembles competitively detect noisy labels and support filtered training; performance depends on training hyperparameters and checkpoint selection, with no universally best variant.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines ordinary training on noisy labels as part of a noisy-label detection study; it does not reproduce the claim's benchmark training-error evaluations or compare network size.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the learning-rate scheduler changes when memorization occurs and the usefulness of checkpoints for noise detection. It studies multistep, linear, and restarted cosine schedules.
record.problems: The relevant training-memorization result is qualitative, with no exact training-error values or uncertainty reported. The empirical evaluation reports a single run per setup.
record.rows_left_out: No other results in the paper were extracted as training-error rows; the noise-detection and filtered-training metrics do not measure the claim's training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Training-error outcomes on CIFAR-10, fully random labels, model-size comparisons, Adam, and regularization comparisons are not established. Early checkpoints precede complete memorization, but their exact training errors are unavailable. Random initialization is not explicitly documented for the Section 6 runs.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Depth comparisons, plain versus residual networks, and training without normalization.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its own memorization observations make it a test despite its primary detection objective. Detection scores and filtered test accuracies do not establish training error. Scheduler sensitivity in noise detection does not by itself limit V1 or test V5. Figures are flattened in the supplied text, and the experiments provide no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10 result, random-label condition, model-size comparison, smaller-model result, or early-stopping/regularization comparison for training error. Exact training-error values are not stated.
